conditionality.statement: The conditional / unconditional split has not been extracted from this document.

btr.$note: 2 attachment(s) are listed for this Party's BTR1. 1 of 8 components are evidenced by an attachment name; the rest are unread, not missing. Adaptation and Article 6 are chapters inside the report rather than separate attachments, so no filename can evidence them and both stay unknown for every Party. Submission dates are not in this listing.

vulnerability.$note: From the 2026 bulk release, latest available year. ND-GAIN restates earlier years between releases (Cambodia 2021 read 40.1 in the edition cited by data/khm.json and 40.665 here); rank is not in the bulk file.

series.$note: series.observed holds several sources and must not be read as one curve. DS-35: All greenhouse gases including land-use change, GWP100 (OWID, from Climate Watch / PIK), from 1990. DS-02: Asset-level observed emissions, CO₂e GWP100 (Climate TRACE); land use accounted differently from OWID, 2015-2025. DS-40: Total GHG emissions including LULUCF/LUCF exactly as the Party submitted them to the UNFCCC, on that Party’s own reporting guidelines and GWP set (UNFCCC Data Interface, snapshot of 2024-07-05). Non-Annex I Parties report only the years their national communications cover, and the figure is negative where reported removals exceed reported emissions. Points from an NDC document are that document's own inventory basis. The same year can appear more than once with different values; R3 keeps them side by side and never averages them.

derived.$reason: 35 observed years are loaded, but no NDC target emissions figure has been parsed, so there is nothing to measure the trend against.

country_profile.$note: Population is World Bank SP.POP.TOTL for the latest year published in the 2015–2025 window. Income group is the World Bank's own classification, not a UNFCCC one.

ndc_registry.latest_version: Nationally Determined Contribution of Turkmenistan under the Paris Agreement
ndc_registry.$note: The registry states which submission is current and where it is. It carries no target figure, so nothing in ndc.* is derived from it.

ndc_assessment.vintage: First (I)NDC round, as assessed by WRI CAIT (2016). Not the latest submission.
ndc_assessment.summary: "Turkmenistan considering all acceptable development options and submission of INDC and taking into account national interests and capabilities of the country, as well as analyzing developed by countries INDCs choose the contribution Type 3 (GHG goal/target), which uses a target indicator attached to per unit of GDP. Specific greenhouse gas emissions per unit of GDP are the indicator that can reflect the country's potential to reduce greenhouse gas emissions." "If financial and technological support is provided by developed countries, Turkmenistan could achieve zero growth in emissions and even reduce them up to 2030."
ndc_assessment.ghg_target: Turkmenistan chose an intensity target (taraget indicator attached to per unit of GDP) and communicated that "if financial and technological support is provided by developed countries, Turkmenistan could achieve zero growth in emissions and even reduce them up to 2030".
ndc_assessment.sectors: Energy; Industrial processes; Agriculture; and Waste
ndc_assessment.$note: Third-party assessment of the first (I)NDC round. It is not merged into ndc.*, is not used by derive(), and does not appear on the dial as a target.

ndc_document.$reason: no sentence in this document states an economy-wide percentage reduction against a base year or a business-as-usual projection.
ndc_document.$note: Read by DS-06-NDC from the First NDC as mirrored by openclimatedata; unfccc.int itself refuses this engine's requests. Nothing was accepted from this document.

emissions_profile.$note: Headline totals are OWID only. OWID's CO₂ sub-totals are fossil/industrial CO₂ by fuel, not a full sectoral GHG breakdown, and do not sum to total_mtco2e. DS-05's rows are non-CO₂ gases only and are not comparable with the others; that is also why DS-05 is absent from series.observed, where a shorter curve would read as a disagreement rather than a difference of scope. by_source carries each source whole.

verdict.text: The registry's current submission for this Party is Nationally Determined Contribution of Turkmenistan under the Paris Agreement, filed 2023-01-30. 50 observed values are loaded from DS-02 (11), DS-35 (35), DS-40 (4). For 2024 the sources disagree: DS-02 220 MtCO₂e, DS-35 118.3 MtCO₂e. They are on different inventory scopes and the engine does not reconcile them. No implementation gap is reported: 35 observed years are loaded, but no NDC target emissions figure has been parsed, so there is nothing to measure the trend against. It submitted BTR1. 1 of 8 components have been confirmed in the document; the rest are unparsed, which is not a finding against the country. ND-GAIN scores it 39.4 for 2024. In the first NDC round, WRI's CAIT assessment recorded: Turkmenistan chose an intensity target (taraget indicator attached to per unit of GDP) and communicated that "if financial and technological support is provided by developed countries, Turkmenistan could achieve zero growth in emissions and even reduce them up to 2030". It was classed both. That is a 2016 assessment of an earlier submission, not the target above. Projected warming for 2080-2099 against 1995-2014 ranges from +1.52°C under SSP1-2.6 to +5.31°C under SSP5-8.5. These are model runs, not observations.
